hypothesis: The blind truth is concentrated in pixels that an out-of-fold, catalogue-trained detector ranks at the very top, after published faults are excluded by a 200 m buffer. Tested by holding the geometry (buffer 2 px, spacing 2.8 px, budget 37,654) identical to the owner-reported best file (GEMSDOE32-B2, 0.2778) and changing only the detector, so that any score change is attributable to the detector and not to an untested new geometry.
mechanism: GeoDAWN airborne magnetic and radiometric lineaments, lidar-derived topography and the five addon structural rasters carry a signature of buried structures that is only partly captured by the published USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue. A gradient-boosted model trained on catalogue pixels, scored out-of-fold by quadrant, ranks every eligible pixel by how catalogue-like it is; the top-ranked pixels that are NOT within 200 m of a published fault are the structures the catalogue missed. Dots are thinned to 280 m so no dot spends credit already banked by a neighbour under the 300 m triangular kernel.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Lithologic contact / intrusive margin. A buried magnetic contact beneath apparently uniform radiometric cover produces a lineament in the magnetic and radiometric derivatives that is indistinguishable from a fault scarp at 100 m pixel scale. Because the detector is trained on catalogue faults, it will rank such contacts highly wherever they resemble faulted terrain in the derivative stack. Second candidate confounder: alluvial-fan piedmont flexure (the APFL family already in this repository), which produces a smooth topographic and radiometric gradient that the detector may read as structural. Third: cultural/linear clearing artefacts in the lidar derivatives.

detector.name: refdet / refdet_z
detector.features: 69-layer cached stack (64 static_ABCD + 5 addons), streamed as memmap
detector.out_of_fold_scheme: 4 quadrant folds; for each fold, train on the other three minus a 15 px collar and drop catalogue components touching that training region

design.extrapolation_note: the candidate sits ~15 percentile points above every live anchor in detector rank; this is the single largest source of uncertainty in the estimate

holdout.definition: hide-and-recover: withhold whole catalogue components, derive catalogue-based features from visible faults only, mask visible faults pixel-exactly, score pooled DTI (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel)
holdout.draws: 8 spatially blocked draws, seeds 140 and 141, hide_frac 0.20
holdout.calibration_flag: the holdout ranks B2, the live leader at 0.2778, last of the three (0.00456). The gate is demonstrably mis-calibrated against live scores and should be re-derived before it is used to block further candidates.

estimated_competition_score.evidence_class: COMPUTED - MODEL ESTIMATE, not a score, not ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED
estimated_competition_score.method: two-covariate truth-cell model (distance x detector-quantile) fitted to 17 owner-reported live anchor scores, artefact-level leave-one-out
estimated_competition_score.best_model: step_dead+betapdf, detector dynamic range capped at 1e4
estimated_competition_score.cross_check: hide-and-recover holdout ratio to B2 = 1.94, independently of the truth model
